name: Question 11
problem:
Consider the following differential equation.

$$
2{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x(2x-3){y}^{′}-3y=0
$$

The general solution near $x=0$ of the differential equation above is given by

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{3}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}(3){x}^{n}+{c}_{2}{y}_{2}(x),
$$

where ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ are arbitrary constants and ${a}_{n}(\lambda )$ are coefficients dependent on $\lambda $ (solutions of the indicial equation) and determined by substitution.
Which of the following is the form of the second Frobenius solution ${y}_{2}?$

*Hint: You may assume $x=0$ is a regular singular point of the ODE and the indicial equation of the ODE is $2{\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda -3=0.$*

Consider the following differential equation. 2x2y″+x(2x−3)y′−3y=0 The general solution near x=0 of the differential equation above is given by y=c1x3∑n=0∞an(3)xn+c2y2(x), where c1 and c2 are arbitrary constants and an(λ) are coefficients dependent on λ (solutions of the indicial equation) and determined by substitution. Which of the following is the form of the second Frobenius solution y2?

Hint: You may assume x=0 is a regular singular point of the ODE and the indicial equation of the ODE is 2λ2−5λ−3=0.

a
y2(x)=b−1y1(x)ln⁡x+x−1/2∑n=0∞an(−12)xn
b
y2(x)=y1(x)ln⁡x+x−1/2∑n=0∞an(−12)xn
c
y2(x)=x−1/2∑n=0∞an(−12)xn
d
y2(x)=y1(x)ln⁡x+x3∑n=0∞an(3)xn
e
y2(x)=x3∑n=0∞an(3)xn
